body: Rockstar opened pre-orders on September 24 for the Grand Theft Auto VI: The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection — a premium collector's box priced at $399.99 (€399.99 / £349.99) that ships on launch day, November 19. It contains eleven items. It does not contain Grand Theft Auto VI.

What's inside: a 6-inch Macca the Gator figure with a twist-open stash compartment, matte black Oakley Frogskins with Prizm Sapphire lenses, a New Era 9FORTY snapback, the Leonida Keys crossbody bag, plus a magnetic mirror, a Chunkee the Manatee shot glass, a collectible swizzle spoon, a razor-blade keychain, an enamel pin set, a sticker pack, and a double-sided poster with a full map of Leonida — the last one being the item lore-hunters will be scanning pixel by pixel.

The backlash writes itself: four hundred dollars, no game. But this is entirely consistent with Rockstar's digital-first launch strategy — earlier this year the studio confirmed GTA VI won't get a standard physical release, opting for code-in-a-box instead, a decision that already drew fire from fans and retailers. And they've run this exact play before: the Red Dead Redemption 2 collector's box also shipped without the game.

The real story is what the box signals. The Oakley and New Era collaborations are doing the heavy lifting on that price tag, and "while supplies last" is doing the heavy lifting on urgency. Rockstar has effectively split the traditional collector's edition in two: the game goes digital, the shelf candy goes premium. Whether fans bite at $400 will tell us a lot about how much weight the GTA brand alone can carry — and you can bet Take-Two is watching that number closely.
Pre-orders are live now via the Rockstar Games Store. If the map poster leaks anything interesting, you'll read about it here first.

Rockstar finally speaks: "heartbreaking" leaks, the Collector's box that won't sell out, and a new mod rulebook
body: Rockstar did something it almost never does this week: it talked. After a week in which 14 gameplay videos leaked from a playable build of GTA VI, the studio issued a rare public statement calling the leaks "heartbreaking" for the team — and, in the same breath, apologized for how long everything has taken: "from getting the game finished (nearly there!)" to sharing official gameplay. The key line for anyone counting down: GTA VI is still on track for November 19.

The leaker, operating under the name "Cyberleek," has reportedly been posting clips daily since mid-August — claimed to be a protest against Rockstar's decision to make GTA VI digital-only — while also soliciting cryptocurrency donations to keep the leaks coming. Rockstar's apology is as much a calculation as a confession: with the game eight weeks out, it needs the leaks contained and the hype channelled back into official reveals. It also tacitly admits the obvious: the studio's long silence is partly why the leak economy thrives.

Meanwhile, the Vice City Collection collector's box — that $399.99 shelf shrine we covered on September 26 — has become a talking point for the wrong reason: it still hadn't sold out nearly 48 hours after launch. Fans slammed the £349.99 price for a box with no game inside and no Jason or Lucia merchandise at all, with community member ben (@videotech) calling "£350... a really hard ask" even for a self-described massive Rockstar collector. Rare air: a GTA-branded anything sitting in stock.

On the platform front, The Verge reported that GTA VI pre-orders are heavily skewed toward PS5 — a claim Xbox CSO Matthew Ball answered publicly, saying Xbox is "very happy" with performance, that the game is breaking records on the platform, and that Xbox's pre-order share matches its console market share. A split roughly matching install bases (PS5 nearing 100 million vs. Xbox Series X|S around 35 million) would be expected anyway — but only Rockstar and the two platform holders know the real numbers.

And finally, Rockstar quietly published updated modding guidelines ahead of launch — a rulebook for GTA VI's inevitable mod scene. Creators can't touch official storylines, missions, or characters, can't mash maps or characters from different Rockstar games together, and multiplayer mods are confined to Rockstar's licensed Creator Platform. It's not a ban — the NoPixel RP deal shows Rockstar wants mods — it's the studio fencing the yard before the biggest launch in gaming history.

body: Rockstar doesn't usually chase you — but the Vice City Collection is getting the full-court press. On September 24, the studio sent a dedicated email blast to newsletter subscribers: "Pre-Order The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection Now While Supplies Last," complete with the full collection artwork. For a company that normally lets a logo reveal break the internet by itself, a direct "buy now" email for merch is genuinely unusual.

The timing is pointed. Stock trackers confirmed the $399.99 box was still available for pre-order on September 25 — nearly 48 hours after launch, rare air for anything with a GTA logo on it. Today, the Rockstar Store page shows the box as "COMING SOON." Either the first pre-order allocation quietly closed behind that "while supplies last" framing, or Rockstar is staging the next wave. Either way, the email's job is clear: convert the fence-sitters.

Meanwhile the value debate keeps getting worse for Rockstar. TheShortcut spotted that several items are repurposed from older GTA special editions — the mirror from the original Vice City collector's edition, the swizzle spoon from The Ballad of Gay Tony. And in the purest possible fan response, one X user has already modeled a 3D-printable Macca the Gator figure and is selling the file for €1.50. Four hundred dollars versus a euro fifty: that is the entire controversy in one comparison.
The box remains a Rockstar Store exclusive — one per customer, 11 items, and the game sold separately. If the next pre-order wave opens, you'll read about it here first.

GTA VI just went high fashion: the Love magazine cover, Jason and Lucia's character clues, and the rest of this week's news
body: With 45 days to launch, Rockstar's latest GTA VI beat didn't come from a trailer — it came from a fashion magazine. Love magazine's Issue 27, titled "America's Most Wanted: Grand Theft Auto VI," hits newsstands today (October 5) with the game on the cover and a batch of new screenshots: Jason and Lucia in a restaurant booth, a backyard hangout, and a neon-lit Vice City moment. No gameplay, no new trailer — but a deliberate one. Rockstar is clearly saving its final surprises for launch while keeping the news cycle fed on atmosphere: the Netflix Extended Look, the Game Informer cover, and now this. At this stage of the countdown, marketing is about mood, not mechanics.

The real content is in how Rockstar talks about the leads. Jason and Lucia are "vulnerable, tough, flawed" and "perfectly imperfect," and their crime spree is described as "hopeful and naive." That's the language of a love story, not the series' usual pitch-black cynicism — and Rockstar confirms Lucia is the series' first fully voiced female protagonist. The satire target has also sharpened: instead of chasing yesterday's headlines, GTA VI is aiming at influencer culture, internet behavior, and everyday digital weirdness, while Leonida is billed as the biggest, most densely packed map Rockstar has ever built — roughly twice GTA V's size, with hurricanes and more than 170 animal species. It all points to the Red Dead Redemption 2 playbook: emotional stakes up front, world density as the selling point, systems to be discovered on day one.

Two more launch-checklist boxes got ticked this week. The ESRB has officially rated GTA VI M for Mature (blood and gore, intense violence, nudity, strong sexual content, drugs and alcohol, plus in-game purchases), matching the PEGI 18 classification in Europe. Neither rating is a surprise, but ratings only land once the game's content is effectively final — so this is another quiet signal that the November 19 date is locked. Meanwhile, dataminer PlayStation Game Size reported on October 2 that the PS5 launch build requires system software 14.10.00.00 — which Sony rolled out on October 1. Unconfirmed: neither Rockstar nor Sony has commented, and datamines have been wrong before. But the practical takeaway stands: if your PS5 has been offline, update it well before launch day.

And the Housers? Co-founder Sam Houser pulled out of a GQ interview he'd been setting up for four years, citing personal reasons — and Dan Houser, Rockstar's former lead writer, told Variety he's deliberately avoiding GTA VI entirely so it doesn't "distract or disrupt" his creative work at Absurd Ventures. Nobody's suggesting drama; it's just Rockstar being Rockstar — famously private, letting the game do the talking. But with the most anticipated release in years now six weeks out, even its creators' silence has become part of the story. Tick tock: 45 days. The countdown continues on the homepage.

posts.title: Cyberleek's $30 million ultimatum: a 'playable build' for a memecoin, and the radio stations that actually matter
body: Unverified — treat everything in this paragraph as a claim, not a fact. Cyberleek, the group behind two months of unauthorized GTA VI clips, has escalated: in a message surfaced this weekend, it says that if its own memecoin reaches a $30 million market cap, it will release a working build of GTA VI — "full story mode, played to the end, credits and all." The stated "one way out" for Take-Two: physical discs and a public apology. IGN notes it's unclear whether Cyberleek means a genuinely playable build or simply a full video playthrough — a categorically different thing. Rockstar and Take-Two have confirmed neither the build's existence nor the leaker's identity, and Indy100 reports the coin collapsed again shortly after the demand surfaced. What Take-Two has confirmed is its hunt: it told a court its efforts to identify the leaker are "rapidly evolving," has filed multiple subpoenas to Discord, and withdrew a YouTube subpoena it no longer needs. With 38 days to launch, this is blackmail-by-memecoin: maximal drama, minimal trust. Watch for it, but don't bet your countdown on it.

The verified big news is the music. Rockstar officially revealed the first six GTA VI radio stations this week: Cocoteo FM (Latin), Back Country Radio (renegade country), AfroBank FM (African music), The Chamber 106.6 (metal), the returning Flash FM, and Dirty South Classics (regional rap and hip-hop) — with three new screenshots of Leonida alongside. Radio in GTA has always been the secret worldbuilding engine, and with names like Mud Dog Mike, the swamp meteorologist, Rockstar is signaling the same satirical density here. But here's the real headline: for the first time in any Rockstar game, Jason and Lucia can listen to radio and on-demand podcasts on foot, through headphones and earbuds connected to their in-game smartphones. Rockstar frames it as part of the social-media-era world — you can follow accounts, tune into podcasts, and stay plugged in while walking Leonida. It also quietly reframes the satire target: the station list is diverse, but the form of GTA's media critique is catching up with how everyone actually consumes audio in 2026.

The podcasts aren't the only detail that deepens the simulation picture. Rockstar's senior VP of narrative, Rupert Humphries, told Love magazine the studio has a dedicated team of pedestrian dialogue writers in Los Angeles — plus separate advertising and comedy writing teams across New York, LA, and London. As open-world writing director James Horton put it: "No one you meet is an extra; they're not only full characters, everyone you meet is the main character in their own story." This is the Red Dead Redemption 2 playbook taken further: the last 60 hours before launch-week marketing will be fought on density — how alive Leonida feels — not on new trailers. If NPCs really do have that much writing, the difference between foreground and background is just where you're looking.

And a quick cleanup on last week's biggest mix-up: Microsoft's gaming CEO floated that Xbox was doing something around GTA VI that "no other platform holder is doing," which the internet took to mean exclusive PC streaming via Xbox Cloud Gaming. Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball shut that down on October 7: GTA VI will not be streaming exclusively or to PC. The cloud deal is non-exclusive — and it's on consoles only. No PC date exists. Which, for PC players, is its own kind of news: the streaming loophole to play GTA VI on a PC at launch never existed.

One more quiet milestone: today is exactly one month until pre-load. Pre-ordered copies unlock for download on November 12, a week before the November 19 launch. Thirty-eight days, Leonida. The countdown's on the homepage.
